title: My new neighbor keeps returning things he says he borrowed from me. I've never lent him anything.
story:
The first was a ladder. He knocked on a Saturday morning, smiling, and leaned it against my porch. "Thanks for this, you saved my life." I'd never owned a ladder. He was gone before I could say so.

Then a casserole dish, washed. A flashlight. A rake. Each time, the same smile, the same thank you, and every time, I had never seen the thing before.

I started keeping them in the garage. The pile grew. A winter coat. A pillow. A toothbrush, still in the package.

I finally went over to his house to clear it up. His door was open. Inside, it was completely empty. No furniture. No boxes. Just a long list taped to the kitchen wall, in neat handwriting, with a check mark next to almost every line.

Ladder. Dish. Flashlight. Rake. Coat. Pillow. Toothbrush.

At the bottom, one line without a check mark. It just said my address.

I ran home. Everything he'd returned was still in my garage, stacked neatly, and I finally understood what the pile was. He hadn't been returning things.

He'd been moving in.

My doorbell rang that evening. He stood on the porch with a suitcase.

"Thanks for having me."
premise: neighbor keeps 'returning' items never lent; the pile in the garage is him moving into the narrator's house
